newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack shares shrug off Opraf statement.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack shares shrug off Opraf statement.

text.p: Shares in Railtrack Plc rose in early trade on Tuesday after a statement from the industry regulator Opraf provided no fresh negative surprise for the owner Britain's rail network, analysts said.
The stock -- which has retreated from its record 805p set last week -- was up 15p at 794-1/2 by 0754 GMT in volume of just under half a million shares.
The rail regulator said the proposed license modifications set out a new general duty on Railtrack in respect of maintaining the network and gave new powers of investigation and enforcement.
Yet analysts said the statement added little to previous pronouncements from the regulator and carried little threat to Railtrack's profitability.

"The regulator is only holding the company to what it is keen to tell shareholders it is doing anyway," said Alastair Gunn, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing. "If this is getting tough then people will be breathing a sigh of relief."
